trials.notes: Medium pnpm TypeScript library with "type": "commonjs" and engines.node >=12.20.0. Installs, builds, type-checks and passes its tests, on the host too. The review hit a crash on the commonjs type, a silent host fallback because node:12-bookworm doesn't exist, and with --image a false Level 0 because the audit's pnpm store sat in the work tree and prettier parsed it. Run from the copied skill, the audit currently exits before sealing with "Cannot use import statement outside a module".

pnpm monorepo of 21 packages. The root vitest runs 818 tests, and cli alone has 17 test files, so no package lacks tests. 8 git-tag tests fail in a container only because git has no user identity there, which CI sets.

any.headline: Agents can build and test repository, but its tests can't yet catch wrong changes.

trials.notes: Small npm JavaScript library. Install, lint, build, npm test and npm run test:perf pass. The README's yarn add, pnpm add, prose path and npx dotenv examples are consumer documentation, not wrong agent instructions. scripts/parse-perf.js:25 holds the AWS documentation key AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE, not a committed secret. engines.node >=12 maps to node:12-bookworm, which doesn't exist, so even with Docker the audit falls back to the host without saying why (the same defect as zustand).

any.headline: Agents can build and test dotenv, but its tests can't yet catch wrong changes.

trials.notes: Monorepo of 4 TypeScript npm workspaces and 2 uv Python servers. The TypeScript workspaces install, build and pass 1,747 vitest tests. All 17 instruction findings were false: trailing semicolons kept on script names, a deleted file named in a never-re-add rule, package-relative paths checked from the root, and an example worktree path. 3 of the 6 missed planted faults were genuine gaps; the rest were equivalent mutants or a stale dist/. Each Python server runs in the uv image, so with PyPI reachable it installs and tests on its own; where PyPI is blocked it is unproven on that machine. On an open network the whole instruction replay runs (40 findings at 214d349), and each is explained on its merits. Real: .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md:566 gives `npm run release:notes` with no arguments, and the script exits with "--milestone, --merge-sha, --merge-branch and --ledger-url are all required"; the docs point at the script's header instead of giving them. Environment, blocked with the reason: local:gate, verify:dco, interface-diff and changeset need origin/v2/main, which the one-commit clean copy has no remote for; skills:eval needs the claude CLI; coverage:py runs uv from the Node image. Needs the network: uv --directory src/<server> run and uvx --from download a Python while the replay is offline. Needs access: npm whoami. Skipped as written: the `cd src/<server>` block and `uv run pytest` in `src/<server>` (a folder left to the reader), uv lock in "that server" (one of src/fetch, src/git, src/time, unnamed), a bare `uv run` in prose, `<lower branch>`, ../servers-release outside the repo, the loop's $s, and `node --test` in the table's Runner column. validate, validate:guards and test:scripts pass now that the container reaps orphaned processes (--init); without it two gate-lease tests saw zombies as a live process tree. src/git is Level 1 in the uv trixie image once the audit adds git: with bookworm's git 2.39 its merge-driver test failed, and with the audit's identity in GIT_AUTHOR_* variables 9 tests that set their own identity in a temporary repo failed.

Go backend with 90% of changes, now scored in golang:1.27 (its go line), plus a Svelte and Vite ui/ that builds and has no test script, so ui at Level 0 is correct. The backend builds, and 930 of its 931 top-level tests pass offline; TestRecordAuthWithOAuth2 downloads an avatar from pocketbase.io, and the audit runs tests without the network on every machine, so pocketbase at Level 0 is the honest result. Its CI runs go test only, so go vet isn't run (vet would flag a test fixture's deliberately unexported field). Both earlier blocking private-key findings were false: a Go doc comment and a textarea placeholder. The README's Go tutorial and release-binary commands are not instructions for ui. No instruction is wrong, and none is a finding. CONTRIBUTING.md:48 `go test ./...` and :51 `make test` run the test check's command, so they take its result instead of failing twice. :60 `make lint` is blocked, because golangci-lint, which the guide links to install, isn't in the image. :85 `npm run build` runs in ui, the folder its section starts in, and takes the build check's pass.

Run with no container runtime. agent-readiness installs, type-checks and passes its tests (435 of 436, 1 skipped without Docker), yet the review's audit sealed Level 0, not bootable. With no container the honest result is unproven on this machine. The test fixtures' tokens and the tool's own tests needing credentials are not blocking safety findings. README.md:15 links to cloud-agent, which doesn't exist (the folder is self-hosted-cloud-agent); that one instruction finding is real, and upstream main has the same broken link.

Symfony 8 demo app on PHP >=8.4 (composer:2.11, PHP 8.5), with a committed composer.lock, PHPUnit, PHP CS Fixer and PHPStan. With Packagist reachable it installs frozen (its post-install scripts also fetch importmap assets and the Sass binary), passes its PHPUnit suite, and PHPStan reports 1 error, which holds the commands check. 3 of 5 planted faults are caught. config/packages/framework.yaml:3 and security.yaml:46 are Symfony parameter references (%env(APP_SECRET)%, %kernel.secret%) and aren't flagged; .env.local.demo:3 commits APP_SECRET=not-a-secret--read-the-doc! under a demo-only comment, a value that says it isn't a secret, so it isn't flagged. Where Packagist is blocked the install is blocked and the component is unproven on that machine.

Pure-Ruby gem on Ruby 4.0 (.ruby-version 4.0.3) with a committed Gemfile.lock bundled with Bundler 2.4.8, which Bundler installs and switches to during the frozen install. Rake's test task passes 239 minitest runs, RuboCop and Sorbet (srb tc) pass, and all 5 planted faults are caught. Gemfile.lock lists both x86_64-linux and aarch64-linux, so amd64 and arm64 machines resolve the same gems. Where RubyGems is blocked the install is blocked and the component is unproven on that machine.

A Cargo workspace whose root is also the ripgrep package, with nine member crates under crates/ and a committed Cargo.lock. One component covers the workspace and runs cargo build, cargo test with --workspace in rust:1.97, the newest pinned Rust (no toolchain file). Its CI doesn't run clippy, so there is no lint. All 1242 tests pass offline and the tests catch at least 3 of 5 faults planted in member crates, so Level 2 is correct.

Spring Boot 4 sample on Java 17 with a committed Maven Wrapper. With Maven Central reachable it installs, builds and passes its tests offline in eclipse-temurin:17-jdk (the MySQL and Postgres Testcontainers tests skip without Docker), and all 5 planted faults are caught: Level 2. Where Maven Central is blocked the wrapper can't fetch Maven, so it is unproven on that machine.

JVM-only Kotlin library, a Gradle 9.4 composite build (tests live in included builds) with a JDK 11 toolchain. Gradle 9 needs Java 17 to run, so it runs in eclipse-temurin:17-jdk and the foojay resolver provisions JDK 11 during the build. With the Gradle services and Maven Central reachable it installs, builds and tests offline, and 3 of the 4 planted faults that compiled are caught (one survives, one didn't compile): Level 2. Where they are blocked it is unproven on that machine.

pnpm workspace whose root package.json is the Next.js app (most of the changes), with packages under packages/. The Nov 24 Node sim found the root app neither scored nor listed, shares that ignore it, and a lockfile shown as none.

any.headline: Agents can build and test umami, but its lint command fails and its tests can't yet catch wrong changes.

trials.notes: Go library with five go.mod modules (root, exp, benchmarks, internal tooling, assets). The Nov 24 Go sim found only the root module, with benchmarks recorded as a satellite whose manifest is a test file. CONTRIBUTING.md's `make test` walks every module; with the network cut, the modules beyond the root can't fetch their dependencies, and the audit records that as a failure in two runs of three and as blocked in the third (blame by output regex). Recorded as the failure; the ceiling of 1 false instruction finding is that item.

any.headline: Nothing blocks agents in zap and exp: from a clean checkout they install, build and pass their tests, and their tests caught the planted bugs. Start giving agents work there.

trials.notes: uv Python app with a slow test suite. The Nov 24 Python sim's only finding and next move was rotating four secrets that are an FTP URL f-string and three public API client keys, with advice to gitignore shipped source files.

open.headline: Level 2 couldn't be proved for flexget because the audit's time budget ran out (--budget-total or --budget-component). A rerun where these checks can run can prove it.

trials.notes: Django app (v4.7.6) with pip requirements.txt, a root AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, and skill files. Its tests need Postgres and Redis (CI service containers), so the root can't be proven Level 1 without them. netbox/project-static is a Yarn frontend with lint and type checks but no tests; netbox/translations is regenerated by a bot and is excluded. Covers instruction findings in agent files and a database-backed Python app.

Yarn and Nx monorepo (11.18.0) of about 267 package.json files with nested AGENTS.md, 67 skill files and .cursor/environment.json. CI tests every packages/* SDK through the root Nx task graph, so they are members of the root; each dev-packages/* suite (e2e, node, browser and bundler integration tests) runs from its own folder and needs services or the network. Task-graph builds aren't supported yet.

.NET Aspire reference app: one solution (.slnx, central package management) built and tested from the root. Its functional tests start Redis, Postgres and RabbitMQ through Aspire, so they need Docker. src/ClientApp is a MAUI client built only on Windows; the root package.json is the Playwright e2e harness.

Rails app with a Yarn 4 frontend at the same root and an Aptfile of system libraries, about 10,000 files. rspec needs Postgres, Redis and precompiled assets; yarn test:js runs from the same root. streaming/ is a small Node server with no tests.

About 40 .NET projects in one solution, pinned at a commit whose upstream run-tests job is red on Linux, Windows and macOS: the first truth with a failing clean run. Reproduced in mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0: two test projects don't compile (MigrateRatingLevelsTests.cs CS1061, ConfigurationControllerTests.cs CS7036), so a level above 0 for the root is over-claiming (K2).

System.CommandLine: Azure Pipelines CI, a NuGet.config that clears nuget.org for the public dnceng Azure Artifacts feeds, and a prerelease SDK pin (12.0.100-alpha) that only ./build.sh installs from ci.dot.net, so a stock SDK image can't satisfy global.json. eng/common is Arcade's vendored build scripts and is excluded.

pnpm and Turborepo monorepo (web, worker, packages/shared, a Rust ai-gateway) with 21 AGENTS.md files, 240 skill files and a skills-lock.json, and a .cursor/environment.json with its own Dockerfile. Scanned only: discovery, placement and safety findings at customer size.

uv workspace of about 155 members (airflow-core, task-sdk, every provider on its own), a pnpm UI and Go, TypeScript and Java SDKs, about 15,700 files. Scanned only: discovery and placement at customer size.
154 go.mod modules tied by go.work, with GitLab CI beside GitHub Actions. Scanned only: discovery across many modules and non-GitHub CI.
TypeScript library whose main CI is CircleCI, with CLAUDE.md and .github/instructions/. integration-tests is its own pnpm workspace tested with browsers. Scanned only: non-GitHub CI and agent files.
Small Poetry library, the commit supported.md cites as Poetry's proof; its tests need nothing beyond the install, so this re-verifies that claim.

Django app (uv) beside a root package.json that only holds release-it for version bumps and is no project. Its unit tests need Postgres and Valkey. The commit supported.md cites for a Python app next to a root package.json.

Ruby gems (core, api, emails, dashboard, providers) each tested from its own folder, beside a pnpm and Turborepo workspace of JS packages tested through the root task graph. No Gemfile.lock or .ruby-version. The commit supported.md cites for task-graph builds, which aren't supported yet.
Kickstarter's Xcode iOS app with Swift packages, tested only on macOS with a simulator (CircleCI). No supported ecosystem, so the honest result is no level and "needs macOS"; nothing runs.
